source_text: Si castitas virtus est, corpus vero substantialiter malum esset, impossibile erat castum corpus inveniri; quia corpus turpitudinis, virtutis non fieret corpus; cum autem sanctificatur, virtutis efficitur, et ita communicat virtus corpori corpusque virtuti, per quam et templum efficitur Dei. Unde si omne corpus fornicationis esset, impossibile utique erat castitatem in corporibus inveniri: tumque demum naturae corporum possemus malum substantiale deputare. Si vero usque eo corporis merita processerunt, tantoque honore decoratum est, ac tale indumentum pudicitiae suscepit, ut domus sui factoris esse mereretur, ac fieret thalamus Filii Dei, ut venientes Pater et Filius habitationem corporum eligere dignarentur; quomodo non exsecrabilis et ridendus Manichaei sermo convincitur?

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: “If chastity is a virtue, but the body were evil in its very substance, it would be impossible to find a chaste body. A body belonging to shameful conduct could not become a body belonging to virtue. But when it is made holy, it becomes a body of virtue. Thus virtue shares in the body, and the body in virtue; through virtue it also becomes God’s temple (1 Corinthians 6:19). If every body belonged to sexual immorality, it would certainly be impossible to find chastity in bodies. Only then could we count evil as belonging to the very nature of bodies. But if the body has attained such worth, has been adorned with so much honor, and has put on such a garment of purity that it deserves to be its Maker’s house and becomes the bridal chamber of God’s Son—so that the Father and the Son are pleased to come and choose bodies as their dwelling (John 14:23)—how can the Manichaean claim fail to be exposed as detestable and absurd?”

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Glossary: avoid modern merit-theology; Julian means deserved outcome.
